body.statement: For which response-pattern families and finite product orders does the signed incidence system \(\mathfrak H_R\) admit a network-matrix or balanced-hypergraph representation that reduces both joint endpoints to a single polynomial-size min-cut or submodular-flow problem, returns an extremal completion and cross-world coupling, and yields an integral explanatory certificate when \(H_a\) is rational? Establish a necessary-and-sufficient structural characterization or prove a non-representability frontier.
body.justification: The generic linear program certifies sharpness, but a structural frontier would identify exactly when clinicians can receive cut-like explanations rather than opaque dual vectors.
body.gap: Strassen-type transport networks cover fixed marginals, whereas overlapping missing-data projections create hyperedges whose network representability is not characterized by the cited causal or missing-data results.
body.consumer: Software for prespecified multivariate trial endpoints could automatically select a transparent min-cut certificate when the response design permits one and otherwise report why a generic linear-program certificate is unavoidable.
